- When sentiment is high (≥0.6) and forecast is below recent highs, adjust upward to reflect bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is low (≤0.3) and forecast is above recent lows, adjust downward to reflect bearish sentiment.  
- Avoid over-forecasting spikes: if price spikes >10% from prior peak, reduce forecast by 5–10% to account for overreaction.  
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is 5–10% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 2–5% unless sentiment supports continuation.  
- Lag correction: if forecast is 2–3 days behind recent trend, add 1–2% to forecast to account for lagged momentum.  
- Horizon-specific: for 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is volatile (±0.35 in 3-day window), reduce forecast variance by 10–15% to avoid overfitting.
